body:
PROBE currently parses in cyclotron lattices but produces no crossing output. This implements passive cyclotron segment diagnostics and supports collecting turn profiles during coasting and accelerating space-charge runs. Refs #615. This PR covers cyclotron-sector and native RING/FFA particle tracking, with native laboratory probe output and a general coordinate-frame adapter. ## Changes - Observe accepted particle endpoints across finite segments in the laboratory X–Z plane, in both directions. Diagnostic histories follow particle IDs through compaction and MPI migration without changing particle states, fields, reference motion or step scheduling. - Write HDF5/ASCII crossing records. Cyclotron output additionally provides cumulative radial `.hist` / per-reference-turn `.peaks` summaries; FFA output contains phase-space records only because its ring centre may be translated. Flush every 100 accepted steps, at completion and before reporting a collective SINGLEGAP transport failure. Keep fresh-output checks and reject unsupported restart/continuation. - Select coasting cyclotron sectors conservatively from current bunch bounds, preserving native field support checks. This fixes the periodic path-index omission that caused the approximately 23 m particle/reference separation in the ten-turn test. - Extend SINGLEGAP tracking to one unpolarized positive-proton bunch with PIC self fields. MIDPOINT uses a ballistic predictor and frozen-field Boris half kicks around external transport; PRESTEP remains available. Localize the reference stopping duration before prediction/gather and preserve complete RF kicks and the established single-particle endpoint convention. - Share mapped field kernels, include all three momentum components in RF energy balance, and report field-support/RF-kick failures with particle ID, time and laboratory state. - Consolidate selection/descriptors in `DeviceExternalField` and RF event ordering/localization in `TrackReferenceStep`; PIC orchestration stays in `ParallelTracker`. Add host/device unit coverage and reproducible probe/bunch integration scripts. ## Quick migration guide: old OPAL → OPALX probes Keep the probe as a passive finite segment, but translate its geometry and analysis into the OPALX laboratory frame explicitly. | Old OPAL convention or workflow | OPALX equivalent in this PR | | --- | --- | | Horizontal X–Y plane; vertical Z | Horizontal laboratory X–Z plane; vertical Y. Account for the lattice's actual origin, rotation and signs; swapping axes alone may not place a translated ring correctly. | | `PROBE` endpoint attributes | Keep `XSTART`, `XEND`, `YSTART`, `YEND` in **mm**. In OPALX, the legacy `Y*` attribute names specify **laboratory Z**, not vertical Y. Transform detector endpoints before writing the input. | | Probe placement associated with ring geometry | Endpoints are global laboratory coordinates and do not inherit magnet placement. Include each detector once; magnetic symmetry does not replicate probe stations. | | ASCII/HDF5 analysis | `ASCIIDUMP=TRUE` writes `OUTFN.loss`; otherwise use `OUTFN.h5`. Native positions are **m**, momenta **p/(mc)**, and time **s**. ASCII columns are `x y z px py pz id turn bunchNumber time`. | | Radial profiles/peak summaries | Cyclotron sectors provide `.hist` and `.peaks`. Native RING/FFA probes provide phase-space crossings only; calculate radii about the chosen physical ring centre in analysis. | | `WIDTH` / `STEP` | `WIDTH` is retained but unused; there is no vertical clipping. `STEP` is a positive cyclotron histogram bin width in mm, not a tracking timestep or probe sampling interval. | | Comparing turns or row numbers | Match station, particle ID, bunch and time. OPALX `turn` is the zero-based shared reference-return count at the accepted step's start, not a per-particle crossing count. HDF5 `Step#` groups are flush batches, not turns. | Example: a segment at laboratory X=0, covering laboratory Z=4000–4500 mm: ```opal P1: PROBE, XSTART=0, XEND=0, YSTART=4000, YEND=4500, OUTFN="PROBE1"; // Include P1 once in the RING/lattice. ``` For existing analysis that expects a different Cartesian frame, keep native output canonical and convert it afterward. The general adapter in the published PR uses an explicit origin `o` in laboratory metres and an orthonormal matrix `B` whose rows are the target axes: ```text r_target = B (r_lab - o) p_target = B p_lab ``` For example, **if** the desired frame has origin laboratory (-4.42,0,0) m and axes laboratory X,Z,Y: ```sh mkdir -p analysis python tools/probe_frame_adapter.py native/PROBE1.h5 analysis/PROBE1.loss \ --origin-m -4.42 0 0 --basis 1 0 0 0 0 1 0 1 0 ``` This example gives `(x+4.42,z,y)` and `(px,pz,py)`; it is not a universal ring conversion. Use the origin/basis for your lattice. The utility accepts native ASCII or HDF5, requires NumPy/pandas/h5py, preserves IDs/bunch/turn/time, and refuses to overwrite an existing output. It is an optional analysis utility, not a native unit-test dependency. Expect small timestep-dependent differences from old OPAL: OPALX interpolates bracketed accepted endpoints, suppresses initial on-plane hits and duplicate jitter crossings, and observes both crossing directions. A coordinate transform does not reconcile different turn counters or reconstruct hidden intra-step recrossings. Compare chronological passages and timestep convergence rather than requiring identical file rows. Use fresh output basenames; probe restart/continuation remains unsupported. See the [probe guide](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/blob/ce744ef45cab9906a6b713d0b293aa5f3c609151/docs/probes.md) and [adapter usage](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/blob/ce744ef45cab9906a6b713d0b293aa5f3c609151/tools/probe_frame_adapter.md) at the published PR revision. ## Validation - OpenMP build and clang-format 21.1.8 checks pass. - All 10 focused CTest targets pass, including `TestCyclotronSectorMPI` and `TestCyclotronProbeMPI`. Coverage includes bidirectional/finite crossings, repeated HDF5/ASCII flushing, empty ranks, 3D RF kicks, individual arrival times, RF event ordering/ties and failure diagnostics. - Probe integrations pass ten-turn coasting closure, ON/OFF passivity, HDF5/ASCII output and invalid-input checks. Accelerating-bunch checks pass negligible-charge equivalence and one/two-rank comparisons. - Consolidation preserves all ten short integration cases exactly. A 2,000-step single-thread old/new PIC comparison is also exact. - The full 8³-grid / 4,096-particle run reaches the 580 MeV target after a complete kick (reference 580.470767685 MeV, time 22.0354053688 µs). It retains 4,049 particles and 759,907 probe hits. Saved reference states, lost IDs, per-turn counts and the last eight turns' 0.1 mm density bins match the pre-consolidation run exactly. - Four-thread full-run particle coordinates differ by at most 2.39 nm; strict bitwise equality does not pass. The frozen baseline also varies between four-thread repeats, consistent with multithreaded PIC roundoff. No numerical tolerance was widened. ## OPAL–OPALX comparison: final eight turns OPAL 2022.1 (LF2/FFT) versus OPALX (Boris/MIDPOINT PIC), for turns 178–185 (zero-based) in the 580 MeV reference window. Both runs start with 4,096 particles on an 8³ mesh at 2 mA. Profiles use common 0.1 mm bins and physical charge, exclude ID0, and are not area-normalized. The upper panel sums the eight radial line densities; the lower panel shows each turn's mean radius ± rms. ![OPAL 2022.1 versus OPALX: summed radial density and per-turn mean radius for turns 178–185](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e88843b0-98ef-4384-b585-3e34febb449d) Maximum per-turn mean-radius difference: 1.058 mm. OPAL/OPALX rms-width ratio: 0.831–1.112. OPAL retains 4,096 particles, versus 4,049 for OPALX; plotted counts after excluding ID0 are 4,095 for OPAL and 4,051/4,048 for OPALX. Integrator/self-field ordering and particle-removal rules differ, so this coarse single-bunch comparison demonstrates qualitative agreement rather than converged validation.
Individual profiles for all eight turns ![OPAL 2022.1 versus OPALX: individual radial line densities for turns 178–185](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/667f7c57-6c0b-428a-bd12-047c1b2f2bac)
## Limits and follow-up A100 shared-Release native probe tests and small one-/two-GPU FFA comparisons have passed; these are correctness checks rather than production-scale PIC benchmarks. The collective split is a thin-gap approximation and this coarse run is not a mesh/timestep convergence study. It transports one bunch without neighbouring-turn/bunch space charge or a septum model; vertical RF focusing is not included. Restart/continuation and larger probe performance optimizations remain deferred. The earlier 16³ run's failure near 584 MeV cannot be reconstructed from its missing buffered state. Periodic flushing and classified failure diagnostics improve future diagnosis; the successful 580 MeV run does not claim to resolve that failure. User/physics manual edits are prepared in the separate manual checkout and are outside this source-repository PR. ## Failure storage and unit-test stability Commit `648ce4ea5` adds the reviewed tracker cleanup and fixes the remaining unit-test failures. - Replace the per-particle, per-step RF diagnostic array with one persistent failure record per MPI rank. Only failing particles attempt an atomic claim; the successful claimant writes a coherent particle ID and diagnostic payload. The host reads the record after kernel completion. Storage is constant per rank instead of proportional to the local particle count. Selection is the first device claimant rather than the lowest local particle index. - Share the cyclotron field-support predicate between scalar and device evaluation, including consistent rejection of nonfinite positions. Consolidate common RF validation and immutable lattice preparation while keeping the device kernel in the existing public integration method for NVCC. - Fix parallel test interference: the single-rank and MPI loss-data fixtures could delete each other's HDF5 files, and the static/dynamic FM2D fixtures shared a temporary directory. Give generated maps, checkpoints, diagnostics, reference paths and spectrum CSVs owned directories. A shared native C++ helper atomically claims directories, broadcasts shared paths and creation errors within MPI jobs, and leaves cleanup to the owning rank after writers close and peers synchronize. Remove deletions of files the fixture never created. CMake/CTest parallel scheduling remains unchanged; no external scripts or data dependencies are added to native unit tests. - Replace the Gaussian test's invalid fixed `5.5σ` maximum with Bernstein exceedance-count checks and a sample-size-dependent normal maximum. Split an explicit `10⁻⁶` false-alarm budget between the new tail-check families; the existing RMS checks retain their own thresholds. Keep the sampler, seed, 100,000-particle sample and strict longitudinal cutoff unchanged, and check all six components for finiteness. Validation of the published fixes: - **137/137 CTest targets pass** locally with OpenMP and on Linux Debug/OpenMP. - All 29 output-isolation targets pass; 20 concurrent FM2D pairs pass, and five explicit two-/four-rank checks pass with 18 native case executions and zero skips. - Gaussian coverage passes on one/two ranks with one/four threads: 48 native case executions, zero skips. All seven distribution targets pass. - Focused A100 tracker/RF/probe coverage passes 111 case executions. Four CPU bunch comparisons are byte-identical before/after the tracker cleanup, and actual GPU tracker success/failure checks pass on one/two ranks. This A100 coverage applies to the tracker subset; it is not a fresh CUDA validation of every subsequently isolated fixture. GPU tracker integrations use `TYPE=NONE` and zero charge; charged PIC comparisons run on CPU. Larger probe synchronization, history-storage and summary-output optimizations remain deferred to #674. ## OPAL vs. OPALX: 16-cell FFA probe comparison The original `FFA25_OPAL.ipynb` example was run with OPAL 2022.1 and the PR's OPALX build: one proton at nominal 12 MeV, 16 probe stations, no space charge, and the same physical launch and tracking duration (7.36532 µs). **All 199 positive-time crossings match by station, particle ID and chronological passage, with no missing or extra crossings.** OPALX one- and two-rank results are identical, including probe records and final particle/reference states. **Coordinate and lattice conversion.** Old OPAL uses horizontal `(x,y)` and vertical `z`; native OPALX uses horizontal `(X,Z)` and vertical `Y`. For this ring, the matching map is `(X,Y,Z) = (x−4.42 m,z,y)` and `(PX,PY,PZ) = (px,pz,py)`. The comparison converts native output back to the old frame; native probe files remain unchanged. Physical magnet placement also accounts for the legacy clockwise ring convention: entrance angle `π/2−φ_template−L/R0`, reversed spiral handedness, and reversed magnetic-field sign under the axis reflection. **Remaining differences.** Maximum radial-position difference is **35.8 µm** (RMS **14.5 µm**), maximum radial-momentum difference is **1.41×10⁻⁵ p/(mc)**, and maximum crossing-time difference is **5.74 ps**. The residuals are nonzero and grow with tracking duration. Old OPAL uses RK4 and legacy crossing extrapolation/current-step momentum; OPALX uses its native transport, boundary subdivision and endpoint interpolation. Legacy ASCII also has six significant digits. Two old OPAL initial-plane records at `t=0` are excluded because OPALX suppresses initial on-plane hits. Turn labels are retained separately: the old example's “7 turns” is a 1 MHz step covering about 12 geometric revolutions plus a partial thirteenth, whereas OPALX counts reference particle returns. Both runs stay in the midplane, so this example does not validate vertical dynamics or space charge. ## ScalingFFA meshes and passive probe planes ScalingFFA magnets have their own display category and teal nominal bodies with logarithmic spiral faces. Zero-field design arcs are neutral outlines. The 16 passive PROBEs appear as translucent grey planes in native laboratory coordinates; their 1 m height is for display only and does not restrict detector acceptance. ![ScalingFFA nominal bodies and grey passive probe planes, viewed from above and in perspective](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/89e300eebf869d46b8e1a72741406b2716a3a4ca/docs/validation/probes/scaling-ffa-probe-planes.png) Six native mesh tests pass, and the generated viewer works. Full one- and two-rank example runs retain exactly unchanged probe records and final particle/reference states. Follow-up: [#676 — Review visualization of passive PROBE elements and its coupling to ParallelTracker](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/issues/676). The current tracker adds already-global detector planes only to the display mesh; the issue investigates a shared export layer that keeps visualization responsibilities out of tracking while preserving passive-element separation. ## Deferred performance work 1. Tracked in #674: batch station communication, compact migratable endpoint histories and batch cumulative cyclotron summaries, with follow-ups for lattice metadata caching and large-file adapter memory. These changes remain separate from this PR's crossing/output correctness work. 2. Understand the increase in errors between OPAL and OPALX.
title: Implement cyclotron PROBE and accelerating space-charge tracking
